synthetic_power_sensitivity_analysis.methodology: Analytical asymptotic power calculation under AR(1) error persistence and Newey-West HAC variance adjustment

key_analytical_findings.description: When true alpha equals the hurdle (mu = 10 bps), power against the 10-bps hurdle is mathematically identical to alpha (5.00%). Claiming high power when true alpha equals the hurdle is a statistical error.

At N_def = 30 with moderate serial correlation (rho = 0.20), effective sample size collapses to N_eff = 20.0. If true effect is 15 bps (5 bps above hurdle) with std = 50 bps, power against the 10-bps hurdle is only 11.55%. At true effect = 20 bps (10 bps above hurdle), power is 22.65%. To achieve ~38% power, true effect must reach 25 bps (15 bps above hurdle).

Power against a zero hurdle (mu > 0) is substantially higher than power against the economic hurdle (mu > 10 bps). For N_def = 30, rho = 0.20, std = 50 bps, power against zero is 84.1% for mu = 15 bps, whereas power against the 10-bps hurdle is only 21.2%.

To achieve institutional power (>= 80%) against an economic hurdle of 10 bps with a realistic true alpha of 15 bps and std = 50 bps, sample size must reach N_def >= 120 (or N_def >= 60 if true alpha is >= 20 bps).
